methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops delivered by a Norfolk native directly target the technology gap through grassroots peer education, representing distributed capability-building outside traditional institutional channels—a key marker of the 'Build It Yourself' pathway emerging in a non-metro hub.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's partnership with AI Ready RVA concentrates institutional AI education infrastructure in Richmond, creating a metro hub for innovation that risks deepening rather than bridging the capability gap with rural Virginia unless accompanied by distribution mechanisms.

signals.title: Tech Briefs: New bill backed by Warner would curb energy costs, demands from data centers
signals.signal_reading: While the ARC grant for Radford's AI workforce study signals attention to rural challenges, a study alone represents shallow engagement—the gap between researching AI's workforce impact and building actual distributed AI capability reveals the risk of analysis without implementation.

signals.title: Children’s National and Virginia Tech deepen pediatric AI collaboration to accelerate innovation for children - Children's National Hospital
signals.signal_reading: Children's National and Virginia Tech's pediatric AI collaboration deepens technical expertise in Blacksburg, but the specialized, research-focused nature concentrates cutting-edge AI capability in a university setting rather than distributing practical fluency across the broader regional workforce.

signals.title: UMW Launches Virginia’s First Master’s Degree in AI in Business - University of Mary Washington
signals.signal_reading: UMW's launch of Virginia's first AI business master's degree creates formal credentialing that could concentrate advanced AI capabilities among those with access to graduate education, potentially widening the gap between credentialed professionals and workers needing just-in-time AI fluency for job adaptation.
